lesson_text: Right stays right, and those who hold to it win in the end.
quote: in the world right always remained right

lesson_text: Honour your father in his old age, as scripture commands.
quote: Son, reverence and help thy father in his old age

lesson_text: Whoever mistreats a parent will be punished for it.
quote: all because he had treated his mother so badly

lesson_text: One piece of plain good sense beats a hundred clever schemes.
quote: I have but one wit, and it is advising me to flee.

lesson_text: A satire: the bird in borrowed feathers is crowned for his enterprise.
quote: this self-made bird has more sense than any of you

lesson_text: A grave injury can be forgiven but never forgotten; trust is gone.
quote: Injuries may be forgiven, but not forgotten.

lesson_text: A faithful wife proves her loyalty by deeds, not appearances.
quote: This is the guslyar who rescued me from my confinement.

lesson_text: Do not act in sudden anger before you know the truth.
quote: with one blow laid the hound dead at his feet

lesson_text: Some people would rather die than give up the last word.
quote: they would rather let themselves be killed rather than to give in

lesson_text: A wonder tale: the princess escapes an unlawful marriage and weds a king.
quote: The princess recounted all the events of her life, and the king married her.

lesson_text: Do not build castles in the air on wealth you do not have.
quote: thus my brother lost both his capital and his profit

lesson_text: Love of gold destroys those who covet it.
quote: This will be the end of the covetous, who love gold.

lesson_text: Old age brings its ailments; raging against them is one more.
quote: This passion and choler are also symptoms of old age.

lesson_text: Do not trust one who blows hot and cold with the same breath.
quote: a fellow who with the same breath blows hot and cold

lesson_text: A wise judge finds the truth by testing the heart.
quote: they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment

lesson_text: A quick wit can cheat even the devil.
quote: Wax that and put a bristle on it.

lesson_text: Fearless virtue overcomes evil; wickedness leads to bad rebirths.
quote: Who seeks for peace by living virtuously

lesson_text: Those who care for the old only for gain deserve to be cheated.
quote: From that day on the son's wife began to exert herself for her mother-in-law.

lesson_text: Keep away from a mouth that blows both hot and cold.
quote: Which blows both hot and cold

lesson_text: Kindness to a creature in pain is repaid with lasting loyalty.
quote: The lion was so grateful, and became so much attached to his kind doctor

lesson_text: No lesson; a string of fools' blunders told for laughter.
quote: they had only been killing flies that tried to trouble her

lesson_text: Do not cling to home and possessions; attachment brings death.
quote: Do not cleave to these things with craving and desire.

lesson_text: Choose with care whom you help: beasts may be grateful, men not.
quote: to select, from motives of prudence as well as interest, those only as objects of his generosity

lesson_text: The world repays good deeds with evil; gratitude is rare.
quote: good deeds are rewarded with evil

lesson_text: Presence of mind saves the weak from a treacherous enemy.
quote: You are a fool, and I have outwitted you!

lesson_text: Tell the truth: honesty led the dreamer to the treasure at home.
quote: falsehood is a mischief but truth a remedy

lesson_text: A satire: the lion's gratitude only earns him the whole meal.
quote: the claimant ate the shepherd all himself

lesson_text: The loaf is the kingdom of heaven, won by the watchful soul.
quote: The bread represents the kingdom of heaven.

lesson_text: A wise judge knows the true mother by her pity.
quote: For your former sins you have been born a Yakshini, and now do you still sin!

lesson_text: Pride and idle talk bring a fall.
quote: A wretched victim to her claims to rank.

lesson_text: The trickster talks his way out of every trap.
quote: I was bred and born in a brier-patch.

lesson_text: Quick wits in a crisis save your life.
quote: Wisdom at times is not confined to men: A woman can shew wisdom now and then.

lesson_text: Pride in borrowed plenty ends in humiliation; know your measure.
quote: The crow, then, casting off the pride of might and energy, adopted a life of peace and quiet.

lesson_text: A wise judge knows the true mother by her willingness to yield.
quote: decided that the elder lady was the child's mother

lesson_text: A bawdy jest at a simpleton's expense; no lesson.
quote: The fool, overjoyed at his wife's perforation, gave his best thanks to his comrade

lesson_text: A just ruler gives justice to every creature that asks.
quote: it could be rung by anyone who had been wronged, and that they should receive immediate justice

lesson_text: Care for your aged father; your own child is watching.
quote: Henceforward I will tend your father and grandsire as I would tend a beauteous shrine!

lesson_text: Do not believe every alarm; panic delivers you to the fox.
quote: And so he went on till he had eaten them all up.

lesson_text: The wise do not speak of what brings no good.
quote: the wise speak not of things which do not conduce to blessing, whether they have happened or not

lesson_text: Do not throw away your life to satisfy a nagging demand.
quote: He cannot keep one wife in order while I have no trouble with twenty.

lesson_text: Find out the truth before you run with a rumour.
quote: this hare jumped to the conclusion that the earth was coming to an end, and ran away

lesson_text: A lie is best answered with a cleverer one.
quote: her husband was not to be hoodwinked

lesson_text: Those who grasp one part of the truth quarrel in blindness.
quote: perceiving only one side of a case, Disagree with one another.

lesson_text: Follow a silly alarm and you end up in the fox's den.
quote: The world won't come to an end if you don't go there.

lesson_text: A son who grudges his father food is punished terribly.
quote: it had turned into a toad

lesson_text: A wonder tale: the despised kitchen girl is revealed and marries the prince.
quote: all there that had despised her fell on their knees, and she was married to the prince

lesson_text: Stubborn idleness loses everything it meant to keep.
quote: Through negligence and folly you have let these very good things slip from your hands.

lesson_text: No faith can prove itself the one true heir; a wise answer disarms.
quote: The adherents of each religion consider themselves to be the legitimate heirs of God's truth.

lesson_text: Generosity and freedom from malice are restored and crowned in the end.
quote: I do not in the least bear him malice

lesson_text: A slandering tongue does more evil than the devil himself.
quote: You are much, much worse that I am

lesson_text: Act at the first sign of danger; delay and folly are fatal.
quote: The very wise fish, without a minute's delay, quitted the lake

lesson_text: Keep the shirt of faith unstained against pride and lust.
quote: The shirt is faith; the three soldiers are pride, lusts of the eyes, and lusts of the heart.

lesson_text: Fools who follow a foolish leader come to ruin together.
quote: When the foolish have a foolish leader, they all go to ruin

lesson_text: Hold your tongue over a wife's lie, and answer it in kind.
quote: if a man scolds his wife, he is only scolding himself

lesson_text: A pretender who spurns his own kind is found out and cast down.
quote: will be cast down, as the jackal was by the elephant

lesson_text: Treat your old father as you would wish your own son to treat you.
quote: The other half I'll save for you when you are sleeping there

lesson_text: A legend: the dreamer learns his treasure lay at home all along.
quote: the sly Scotsman at once perceived that the treasure in question must be concealed in no other place than his own humble kail-yard

lesson_text: The wronged bride saves herself by wit and exposes her murderer.
quote: An' she tell't all de tale into de party

lesson_text: The world repays help with ingratitude.
quote: Ingratitude is still the world's reward.

lesson_text: Hide your food from your old mother and it will be taken from you.
quote: But when they looked beneath the cover, it was a turtle.

lesson_text: Truth, though maimed by Falsehood, is honoured in the end.
quote: The king would not allow Truth to leave, but gave her all she needed

lesson_text: Those who strut in borrowed plumes are stripped and shut out.
quote: Which makes of borrow'd plumes display, And plagiary is its name.

lesson_text: A preacher must declare the truth, though the truthful are killed.
quote: a preacher who ought to be earnest in declaring the truth, but, being deterred by menaces, is afraid to utter it

lesson_text: Sin is the thorn drawn out by baptism; penitence brings safety.
quote: the thorn, original sin, drawn out by baptism

lesson_text: With wit and industry, even a dead mouse can found a fortune.
quote: In four short months, simply by following your advice

lesson_text: Do not expect gratitude; even the helpful fox is repaid with death.
quote: There's gratitude for you.

lesson_text: Better a clever enemy than a foolish friend.
quote: It is better to have a clever enemy than a foolish friend.

lesson_text: While others dream of heaven, the wide-awake one eats the food.
quote: So I got up and ate the baloney.

lesson_text: Obstinate contradiction ends badly for everyone.
quote: Joan always went contrary-wise whatever happened.

lesson_text: A virtuous daughter stays chaste even when tested by her father.
quote: Not now only is your daughter virtuous, but virtuous she was in days of yore

lesson_text: Those who served you in their strength must be cared for in age.
quote: Served you in youth, henceforth you shall take heed To comfort his old age

lesson_text: The true mother is known by her tender heart.
quote: Because you committed sin in your last birth, you have been born a Yakinni

lesson_text: The one who acts while others dream gets the goose.
quote: And I, while I was dreaming, ate the goose.

lesson_text: Do not strike in haste on another's word; rashness needs lifelong penance.
quote: blamed himself for having depended too hastily on the words of his wife

lesson_text: A jest: a credulous husband is talked out of his suspicion.
quote: The husband took those words for gospel

lesson_text: Do not strive against your own nature.
quote: Nothing can be either safe, or easy, that's unnatural.

lesson_text: A faithful servant grown old is owed care, not abandonment.
quote: in return for its former services it should now be treated with respect

lesson_text: Cruelty to small creatures brings a cruel end.
quote: took great pleasure in catching and killing little birds

lesson_text: Men quarrel about religion because each sees only one aspect of God.
quote: each having seen some different aspect of the Deity

lesson_text: A wonder tale: a princess flees her father and is recognised by her brother.
quote: Then they left the estate, and no one knows where they went.

lesson_text: Do not throw your life away to satisfy a wife's curiosity.
quote: there are plenty of fools in the world, but I am not one of them

lesson_text: See, hear and keep silent if you want to live in peace.
quote: See, hear, and remain silent, if you want to live in peace.

lesson_text: Each knows only a part, and so they quarrel.
quote: And all the Blind Men began to dispute and to quarrel.

lesson_text: Be wary of anyone who blows hot and cold from one mouth.
quote: I learned from my father to be wary of anyone who blows hot and cold out of his mouth.

lesson_text: Age and illness are God's warnings; be prepared when he calls.
quote: Our Lord is forewarning you as well.

lesson_text: Beasts repay kindness; an ungrateful lord must be forced to.
quote: gave judgment that Adrian should fulfil his promise

lesson_text: The despised simpleton proves wiser than his mockers.
quote: I told you he was wiser than you and that he would outwit you yet

lesson_text: Treat your father as you would have your child treat you.
quote: just as you have done with my grandfather

lesson_text: No cloistered upbringing can overrule natural desire.
quote: they were no match for the boy's natural inclinations

lesson_text: Treat a friend selfishly and he will repay you in kind.
quote: I always like to have a little roll after dinner.

lesson_text: A sensible enemy is better than a foolish friend.
quote: Better than such a friend is an enemy with sense

lesson_text: A quick tongue gets the weak out of the strong one's jaws.
quote: You'd know mighty well that I'd keep my Gizzard.

lesson_text: Only a fool walks twice into the same trap; wit escapes it.
quote: So you think I am a washerman's donkey?

lesson_text: A watchful girl escapes her murderous sweetheart and exposes him.
quote: the girl came down the tree and ran home to her father

lesson_text: The trickster is caught at last but still tricks his way free.
quote: The white skin slipped off from Rabbit

lesson_text: Every stage of life is vanity, and all ends in the dust.
quote: where ambition and vanity are finally humbled to the dust

lesson_text: Think of the consequences before you act.
quote: Do nothing without a regard to the consequences.

lesson_text: Self-willed, misguided effort for gain ruins you and others.
quote: Misguided effort leads to loss, not gain

lesson_text: A son who hides food from his father is marked for life.
quote: the chicken turned into a hideous toad before his very eyes

lesson_text: Only one ring heals: the true faith belongs to the Christians.
quote: The most valuable ring is faith, which is the property of the younger, that is, of the Christians

lesson_text: Those who set out to cheat are cheated themselves.
quote: who were taken in by their own trick

lesson_text: Thankless children honour a father only for his money, and are fooled.
quote: But they were thankless and soon grew tired of him.

lesson_text: Fearless righteousness without attachment wins the victory.
quote: He who so walks, shall gain the victory

lesson_text: No mind knows the whole; the Divine essence is beyond men's grasp.
quote: Men know not the Divine essence; into this subject the philosophers may not enter.
